questions.stem:
"Osmosis is the net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration to a region of higher solute concentration. In animal cells, an extracellular solution that is more concentrated than the cytoplasm causes the cell to lose water and shrink; a more dilute solution causes water to enter and the cell to swell."

Which is consistent with the passage?
options: In a dilute external solution, an animal cell shrinks.
Water moves from high to low solute concentration.
A concentrated external solution causes animal cells to swell.
Water moves toward the higher-solute side.
questions.exp: Water moves toward the region of higher solute concentration. A, C reverse the effect; B reverses direction; D is wrong (osmosis is passive).

questions.stem:
"In genetics, a test cross is used to determine whether an individual displaying a dominant phenotype is homozygous or heterozygous. The individual is crossed with a homozygous recessive partner. If any offspring show the recessive phenotype, the tested individual must be heterozygous."

Which is the strongest inference?
options: A test cross always produces a 3:1 ratio.
If all offspring show the dominant phenotype, the tested individual is definitely homozygous recessive.
Observation of any recessive offspring proves the tested individual is heterozygous.
Test crosses can reveal the genotype only of recessive individuals.
Test crosses require a homozygous dominant partner.
questions.exp: Recessive offspring ⇒ the dominant parent contributed a recessive allele ⇒ heterozygous.

questions.stem: (General knowledge) The Italian chemist who proposed a number equal to the number of particles in one mole (~6.022 × 10²³), honoured in the constant's name though he did not measure it, is:
questions.exp: Avogadro's hypothesis (1811) underpins the mole concept.

questions.stem: Six boxes are stacked. Box R is above S but below T. Box U is immediately below S. Box V is at the very top. The order from top to bottom could be:
options: V, T, R, S, U, (and W)
T, V, R, S, U, W
V, R, T, S, U, W
V, T, S, R, U, W
V, U, S, R, T, W
questions.exp: Top→bottom must be: V (top) … T > R > S > U … with the sixth box (W) at the bottom. Only A satisfies V top, T > R > S > U, then W.

questions.stem: All squares are rectangles. Some rectangles are rhombi. Therefore:
options: No valid conclusion about squares being rhombi follows.
questions.exp: The premises do not force a relationship between "square" and "rhombus." (In fact a square is a rhombus by definition, but that's an external fact, not derived from the premises.)

questions.stem: If 5 machines make 5 widgets in 5 minutes, how long does it take 100 machines to make 100 widgets?
questions.exp: Each machine makes 1 widget in 5 min; 100 machines make 100 widgets in the same 5 min. (Classic trick — people intuit 100.)

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 12:30?
questions.exp: Minute hand at 30 min = 180°. Hour hand at 12:30 = 0 + 30/60 × 30° = 15°. Difference = 180 − 15 = 165°.

questions.stem: Pointing to a photograph, Maria says, "Her mother is my mother's only daughter." How is the person in the photograph related to Maria?
questions.exp: "My mother's only daughter" = Maria (since no other daughter). So the photographed person's mother is Maria ⇒ the person is Maria's daughter.

questions.stem: A number is doubled, then 8 is added; the result is 20. The number is:
The mitochondrial matrix is the site of:
questions.exp: Krebs cycle enzymes are in the matrix; ETC is in the inner membrane.

questions.stem: The net reaction of cellular respiration is:
questions.exp: Glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + energy. (B is photosynthesis.)

questions.stem: Which gas is produced by muscle cells during anaerobic respiration in yeast but NOT in humans?
questions.exp: Yeast fermentation: pyruvate → ethanol + CO₂. Human muscle fermentation: pyruvate → lactate (no CO₂).

questions.stem: The inner mitochondrial membrane is folded into:
questions.exp: Cristae increase surface area for the ETC and ATP synthase.

questions.stem: The Calvin cycle of photosynthesis occurs in the:
questions.exp: The light-independent reactions (Calvin cycle) occur in the stroma.

questions.stem: Which is the correct site of the light-dependent reactions?
questions.exp: Light reactions occur on the thylakoid membranes (photosystems, ETC, ATP synthase).

questions.stem: A solution of pH 2 is how many times more acidic than a solution of pH 5?
questions.exp: pH difference 3 ⇒ [H⁺] ratio = 10³ = 1000. (Note: this is really chemistry; appears as biology-flavoured.)

questions.stem: The four levels of protein structure in order are:
questions.exp: Primary → secondary → tertiary → quaternary.

questions.stem: Which monosaccharide is the primary energy source for cells and the product of dietary carbohydrate digestion?
questions.exp: Glucose is the central fuel molecule. (Sucrose, lactose are disaccharides.)

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disaccharide?
questions.exp: Sucrose = glucose + fructose (a disaccharide). Cellulose and glycogen are polysaccharides.

questions.stem: Lipids are largely insoluble in water because they are:
questions.exp: Lipids' long non-polar hydrocarbon chains make them hydrophobic.

questions.stem: DNA differs from RNA in that DNA:
options: Is found only in the cytoplasm
questions.exp: DNA uses deoxyribose and thymine; RNA uses ribose and uracil. DNA is double-stranded; RNA is usually single-stranded.

questions.stem: A population is in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium for a locus with two alleles A (frequency p) and a (frequency q). The frequency of the heterozygote Aa is:
questions.exp: Heterozygote frequency = 2pq.

questions.stem: ABO blood groups are an example of:
questions.exp: A and B alleles are codominant; both dominant to O.

questions.stem: In humans, the normal diploid number of chromosomes is:
questions.exp: 2n = 46 (23 pairs).

questions.stem: The cell-cycle phase in which DNA is replicated is:
questions.exp: DNA synthesis occurs in S phase.

questions.stem: Which vessels have thick muscular walls and carry blood away from the heart under high pressure?
questions.exp: Arteries have thick elastic/muscular walls.

questions.stem: The exchange of O₂ and CO₂ between blood and air occurs by:
questions.exp: Gas exchange is by passive diffusion down partial-pressure gradients.

questions.stem: The hormone secreted by the adrenal medulla in the "fight or flight" response is:
questions.exp: Adrenaline raises heart rate, blood glucose, etc.

questions.stem: The longest bone in the human body is the:
questions.exp: The femur is the longest and strongest bone.

questions.stem: Smooth muscle is characterised by:
options: Lack of striation and involuntary control
questions.exp: Smooth muscle is non-striated, involuntary, spindle-shaped cells.

questions.stem: The organelle responsible for ATP production in animal cells is the:
questions.exp: Mitochondria are the site of oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.stem: Which is the correct sequence of blood flow through the heart, starting from the body?
options: Vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta
Vena cava → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta
Aorta → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary vein
Pulmonary vein → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery
Right atrium → left atrium → right ventricle → left ventricle
questions.exp: Standard pathway: body → RA → RV → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → LA → LV → aorta → body.

questions.stem: Calculate the number of moles in 22 g of CO₂. (C = 12, O = 16.)
questions.exp: Molar mass CO₂ = 44 g/mol; n = 22/44 = 0.5 mol.

questions.stem: What volume does 0.25 mol of an ideal gas occupy at STP (Vm = 22.4 L/mol)?
How many atoms are in 1.5 mol of He?
questions.exp: 1.5 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 9.03 × 10²³. (He is monatomic.)

questions.stem: What is the molarity of a solution made by dissolving 5.85 g NaCl (molar mass 58.5) in water to make 500 mL?
The oxidation number of Cr in Cr₂O₇²⁻ is:
Identify the oxidising agent in: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O.
questions.exp: Cu²⁺ (in CuO) gains electrons → Cu; the species reduced is the oxidiser.

questions.stem: Calculate the pH of a 0.05 M solution of a strong base NaOH (assume full dissociation, 25 °C).
The conjugate base of H₂O is:
questions.exp: Water donates a proton → OH⁻ (its conjugate base).

questions.stem: Which has the greatest first ionisation energy?
questions.exp: Noble gas Ar has the highest first ionisation energy in Period 3.

questions.stem: Which molecule has a linear geometry?
questions.exp: CO₂ is O=C=O, linear (two bonding pairs, no lone pairs on C).

questions.stem: Which intermolecular force is strongest?
questions.exp: Hydrogen bonding is the strongest intermolecular force listed (covalent is intramolecular, not intermolecular).

questions.stem: Increasing pressure on a gas at constant temperature will (Boyle's law):
questions.exp: P ∝ 1/V ⇒ higher P ⇒ lower V.

questions.stem: The structural formula CH₃–CH₂–OH represents:
questions.exp: Two carbons + OH ⇒ ethanol.

questions.stem: In the reaction: AgNO₃ + NaCl → AgCl + NaNO₃, the precipitate is:
questions.exp: AgCl is a white insoluble precipitate.

questions.stem: For a reaction at equilibrium, adding a catalyst will:
options: Increase the rate of both forward and reverse equally; equilibrium position unchanged
questions.exp: Catalysts speed both directions equally; K_eq and position unchanged.

questions.stem: Solve: 2x² − 8 = 0.
Solve: |x − 3| = 5.
Solve: log₂(x) + log₂(x − 3) = 2 (x > 3).
Solve the inequality: x² − 4 < 0.
A right circular cylinder has radius 3 and height 10. What is its volume? (Use π = 3.14.)
A die is rolled once. What is the probability of an even number greater than 2?
questions.exp: Favourable: {4, 6} ⇒ 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.stem: A car accelerates from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 10 s. What is its acceleration?
A 12 V battery drives a current through a 4 Ω resistor in series with a 2 Ω resistor. What is the current?
questions.exp: R_total = 6 Ω; I = V/R = 12/6 = 2 A.

questions.stem: A 3 A current flows for 2 minutes. What total charge passes a point?
A 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s collides with a stationary 1 kg object and they stick together. What is their common velocity?
questions.exp: Conservation of momentum: (2)(3) + 0 = (2+1)v ⇒ v = 6/3 = 2 m/s.

questions.stem: A 4 kg object is dropped (from rest). Ignoring air resistance, what is its velocity after 3 s? (g = 9.8 m/s².)
A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 4 m. What is its speed?
